body:
## Context

PR-A3.1 (W1.5-A3.1 — RLS Spine Convergence, Option B) landed the **expand + dual-context + verify** half of the expand→verify→contract convergence:

- **F-1 fix**: legacy interceptor now stamps RLS identity from `req.user.id` (was the undefined `req.user.sub`).
- **Dual-context expand**: both context paths stamp BOTH GUC namespaces with identical truth per request — legacy `app.current_user_id` / `app.current_user_role` (still authoritative) AND the new A2 namespace `app.user_id` / `app.gym_ids`.
- **New helpers** `app.current_user_id_v2()` / `app.current_gym_ids()` exist (migration `20261220000000_rls_helpers_v2`) but **zero live RLS policies read them yet**.
- **Parity/shadow check** in `withRlsContext` deny-logs `RLS_PARITY_MISMATCH` (no throw) when the two namespaces diverge.

## A3.2 scope (this issue — the CONTRACT step, deferred)

1. Confirm the parity soak shows **zero** `RLS_PARITY_MISMATCH` deny-logs over the agreed observation window.
2. Re-point every live RLS policy from `app.current_user_id()` → `app.current_user_id_v2()` (and gym-scope policies onto `app.current_gym_ids()`), in a reversible/idempotent BEGIN/COMMIT migration.
3. Retire the legacy `RlsContextInterceptor` (`src/common/interceptors/rls-context.interceptor.ts`) and the legacy GUC stamps once no policy reads the legacy namespace.
4. Drop the now-dead legacy helpers and the shadow parity check.

## Exit criteria for A3.1 → A3.2

- Parity soak clean (no mismatch logs).
- New-namespace helpers verified against every policy that will be re-pointed.

Tracking issue referenced from PR-A3.1.
title: W1.5-A3.2 — retire legacy RLS interceptor after parity soak
